title: Birb Hangout
summary: A browser-based 3D place where distant friends inhabit the same room, share music and video, read, play, rest, and fly together - supported by purpose-built tools for evaluating character motion and spatial design.
landingDeck: Birb Hangout turns remote connection into low-pressure co-presence. The lounge keeps people, activities, and shared objects visible in one world while a deliberately mixed realtime architecture synchronizes each behavior at the level it actually needs.
landingHighlights: Combines private invite-code rooms, persistent identity, customizable birds, shared media, reading, trivia, voice, consent-based social interaction, rest, and a seeded multiplayer flight world.
Matches each behavior to an appropriate synchronization model: durable room schemas, transient flight relays, peer-to-peer audio, authoritative media intent, and timestamp-driven ceremonies.
Turns subjective 3D feedback into reproducible evidence through specialist studios, exact-time capture, spatial annotation, blind semantic review, negative controls, and owner-controlled acceptance.
problem: Most remote social products ask people either to keep a conversation going or to commit to the same game. That leaves little room for the quieter, parallel rituals that make physical presence comfortable: reading while someone chooses music, resting near a friend, noticing what others are doing, or joining an activity without taking over the room.
approach: Birb Hangout models the lounge itself as the interface. Players appear as expressive birds, approach visible objects, and move between shared and private activities without leaving the common space. The implementation combines authoritative room state, behavior-specific realtime protocols, procedural flight and terrain, and a rigorous creative-engineering workflow for testing how motion and spatial interactions actually read.
output: A TypeScript social-world system spanning a React 18 and React Three Fiber client, Colyseus room server, typed shared protocol, persistence and upload controls, diegetic media and reading experiences, synchronized social interactions, a shared Dream flight world, specialist 3D studios, spatial annotation, and reproducible visual-review tooling.

methodology.evaluation: The project separates mechanical evidence from visual judgment. Recorded work includes instrumentation of twelve original animation clips, preregistered failure predictions, baseline/candidate/ablation comparisons, exact-time and orbit captures, blind-first semantic review, hash-chained candidate safeguards, specialist studio probes, interaction and multiplayer checks, and owner acceptance as the final authority for subjective quality.
methodology.boundary: The implemented product and evaluation system are supported by source, recorded checks, and a live single-service deployment; population-scale usage, high-concurrency capacity, and universal visual acceptance are separate validation questions.

role: I created and built Birb Hangout, defining its product direction, social experience, realtime architecture, visual language, and evaluation methodology. I designed the player journeys; built and integrated the client, server, shared protocol, activities, Dream, procedural landscape, persistence, deployment, and safety controls; directed character and interaction quality; and developed the studios, spatial annotation, candidate harnesses, and evidence process used to evaluate the work.

pageSections.title: A shared digital place where being together does not require doing the same thing
pageSections.description: Friends enter a private 3D lounge as birds, remain aware of one another, and move naturally among conversation, shared media, reading, trivia, affectionate gestures, quiet rest, and cooperative flight.
pageSections.context: The product is designed around co-presence: each activity adds something legible to the room instead of replacing the room with another disconnected interface.

pageSections.title: Activities are visible rituals that invite participation without demanding it
pageSections.markdown:
The lounge uses familiar spatial objects - a record cabinet, turntable, television, sofa, fireplace cushions, bookshelf, photo frame, light switches, and trivia screen - to communicate what is possible and what another person is doing. A bird carries a selected record sleeve to the turntable. A reader holds an open book while another player remains visible across the room. A sleeping bird stays physically present by the fire.

This diegetic approach makes intention observable through action and location. One person can read while another explores; someone else can sit nearby, join the media experience, offer a hug, or start a game. Focused overlays handle setup such as entering a video or choosing a title, then return the activity to the world.

The result is a product for both active and quiet moods. It gives distant friends and family a digital equivalent of sharing a room: company is the central reward, while the world provides enough structure to make that company easy to inhabit.

pageSections.title: The room is both interface and social context
pageSections.description: Walkable space, seats, screens, shelves, lighting, props, and character placement keep people and activities mutually visible.

pageSections.title: A private room remains coherent from invitation through reconnection
pageSections.description: Identity, ownership, occupancy, and shared state are first-class product behaviors.

items.label: Create
items.title: Open a private room and shape a bird
items.body: Choose a name and appearance, receive a short code in the room URL, and establish a locally stored owner token without requiring an account.

items.label: Invite
items.title: Bring a friend into the same room
items.body: The code resolves an existing Colyseus room; invalid codes are rejected instead of silently creating a duplicate world where friends cannot see each other.

items.label: Rejoin
items.title: Recover the same identity after refresh
items.body: A stable browser client identity reclaims the live bird and the owner token restores host authority, preventing duplicate avatars and unnecessary account friction.

items.label: Share
items.title: Synchronize the facts the room must agree on
items.body: Presence, position, pose, seating, avatar, lights, photos, records, shelves, media, fireplace, games, and Dream membership travel through typed shared state.

items.label: Persist
items.title: Carry the room beyond one connection
items.body: A storage abstraction supports local disk in development and S3-compatible room records and private photo assets when configured.

pageSections.title: Media, reading, games, and ambience are engineered as social objects

items.label: Music and video
items.title: One room-owned media experience
items.body: A shared cabinet, carried record sleeve, turntable, television, authoritative media intent, host token, and real playhead correction keep the physical ritual and browser player aligned.

items.label: Reading
items.title: Private pages, socially visible presence
items.body: PDF pages and a bounded EPUB 2/3 pipeline render crisp local reading while a separate animated book actor remains attached to the bird for everyone else in the room.

items.label: Trivia
items.title: A synchronized result becomes theatre
items.body: The server protects the answer key and broadcasts one ceremony start time; each browser derives the reveal, cards, camera movement, and ejection beats from elapsed time.

items.label: Photos and ambience
items.title: Room memory and atmosphere
items.body: Private photo assets, lighting, switches, fireplace state, and synthesized crackle make the shared space feel owned and lived in without reducing it to a content feed.

pageSections.title: Each behavior uses a synchronization model matched to its social invariant
pageSections.description: The system is intentionally mixed instead of forcing every interaction into one universal state model.

items.label: Durable room facts
items.title: Typed authoritative schemas
items.body: Colyseus schemas and room records hold the shared facts that must survive and remain consistent across players.

items.label: Flight
items.title: Compact transient relays
items.body: High-rate Dream motion travels as validated packets with bounded reconstruction, keeping the durable room snapshot compact and lounge-only clients quiet.

items.label: Voice
items.title: Peer-to-peer media
items.body: The server relays WebRTC signaling but never carries audio; spatial gain communicates distance while keeping a faraway friend audible.

items.label: Ceremonies and gestures
items.title: Shared time and staged protocols
items.body: Trivia uses one authoritative timestamp, while hugs use a server-owned request, readiness, synchronized start, cancellation, expiry, and cleanup lifecycle.

pageSections.title: A hug is a private request and synchronized agreement, not a broadcast emote
pageSections.markdown:
The initiator approaches a nearby bird and sends a private request. The server checks identity, distance, availability, request rate, pair cooldown, and expiry before the recipient sees an accept-or-reject prompt. If accepted, the server computes complementary positions and facing, waits until both clients report ready, and starts one synchronized clip. Movement, timeout, cancellation, completion, or disconnection releases both participants.

The three-context smoke specification checks that the offer and consent prompt remain private while the accepted action becomes visible to the room. The feature includes the complete multiplayer lifecycle: proximity, consent, staging, synchronization, privacy, interruption, and cleanup.

pageSections.title: Rest by the fire opens into a shared, physics-driven flight world
pageSections.markdown:
A bird can settle on a fireside cushion, choose a sleeping posture, remain visible in the lounge, and follow a private three-breath sequence into the Dream. Breathing, stars, camera treatment, and background loading progress together while the lounge body stays asleep. The server authorizes entry only for an eligible napping player, owns one active Dream per room, creates the shared nonzero world seed, and tracks membership.

Inside the Dream, each browser advances its bird through a fixed-step six-degree-of-freedom model. Pitch, roll, wing shape, and discrete flaps feed lift, induced and parasitic drag, gravity, momentum, and coordinated turns. Diving converts altitude into speed; pulling out redirects speed into climb; banking reduces vertical lift. Keyboard, touch, gamepad, and scripted probes resolve to the same control structure.

Remote clients reconstruct a partner from compact motion packets using bounded extrapolation and correction against the same seeded world. The architecture keeps local flight immediate and gives each remote bird a coherent trajectory through the landscape.

pageSections.title: Public elevation data becomes a repeatable world built for browser-scale flight
pageSections.description: The Dream starts from USGS 3DEP elevation and extends it with deterministic systems whose visual and performance consequences can be inspected independently.

items.label: Terrain
items.title: A measured flight-scale range
items.body: A 900-metre elevation window is processed and extended into an approximately 3.8-by-8.8-kilometre environment.

items.label: Structure
items.title: Seeded rivers, banks, islands, and shore
items.body: Repeatable builders create major landforms and landmarks so captures, multiplayer navigation, and visual comparisons can return to the same world.

items.label: Ecology
items.title: Ground color and planted geometry agree
items.body: A normalized six-part cover budget drives canopy, shrub, herb, grass, rock, and soil, avoiding terrain that looks forested without containing a forest.

items.label: Performance
items.title: Detail is concentrated where it earns attention
items.body: Species variation, level of detail, culling, tiling, and concentrated detail pockets deliver distinct silhouettes and discovery at a browser-compatible workload.

pageSections.title: Subjective 3D quality is treated as an observable result with human authority
pageSections.markdown:
The project gives typechecks, transport tests, telemetry, and human visual judgment distinct jobs. High-risk visual work starts from references, keeps baseline and rejected candidates available, records the camera and scene state, and requires owner sign-off. One clearly defective frame can veto a candidate; broad acceptance requires evidence across the meaningful views and motion.

Instrumentation of the original twelve animation clips found roughly 1.3-to-1.5-world-unit boundary jumps in every clip, dead holds in six, and missing anticipation in nine. An instrumented hug experiment preregistered eight likely failures and observed seven. Those findings redirected the work from guessed tuning toward measured mechanisms and showed that earlier gates had been testing the wrong construct.

The resulting harness applies frame-keyed changes to an allowlisted set of rig controls, supports linear, cubic-Hermite, and hold interpolation, captures exact frames and telemetry, and restores the baseline atomically. Candidate rounds require mechanistically different variants, an ablation, registered metrics, negative controls, and retained rejection history. Blind-first semantic review asks an unprimed observer what action appears to happen before revealing the intended action, exposing mechanically valid sequences that still communicate the wrong event.

pageSections.title: A vague visual comment becomes a reproducible engineering artifact

items.label: Isolate
items.title: Open the smallest truthful studio
items.body: Birb, Interaction, Room, Rig, Dream, and Landscape studios import production components, pose functions, builders, and cameras behind development-only routes.

items.label: Observe
items.title: Pause at the meaningful frame and viewpoint
items.body: Exact-time capture, named action-axis cameras, orbit views, frame strips, and telemetry sidecars record what was actually seen.

items.label: Annotate
items.title: Attach the note to scene geometry
items.body: An 11-by-11 raycast grid votes among geometry-derived subjects and stores ambiguity, hit rate, camera pose, scene state, likely subject, alternate hits, and world and subject-local coordinates.

items.label: Compare
items.title: Reopen the same view across candidates
items.body: The saved instruction restores camera and state so baseline, candidate, ablation, and later recapture answer the same visual question.

items.label: Decide
items.title: Keep acceptance with the owner
items.body: Hash-chained safeguards constrain write sets and transition authority, independent observations carry open defects forward, and uncertain subjective judgment returns to the owner for a decision.

pageSections.title: The deployment is treated as a shared service, not an unconstrained local demo

items.label: Build and origin
items.title: One deployable client-server system
items.body: The production Docker image builds the client, server, and shared package, then serves the compiled experience from the same origin to reduce deployment and CORS complexity.

items.label: Uploads
items.title: Bounded private photo processing
items.body: Live-room bearer tokens, file and pixel ceilings, autorotation, resizing, WebP re-encoding, and room quotas constrain user-supplied images before storage.

items.label: Traffic
items.title: Typed and rate-bounded inputs
items.body: Production room budgets, keyed network hashes, payload caps, validated message types, and invalid-message counts limit accidental and abusive load.

items.label: Persistence
items.title: Replaceable room and asset storage
items.body: A shared abstraction supports local development and S3-compatible records and assets while keeping persistence separate from realtime room logic.

pageSections.title: Birb Hangout advances both the social experience and the way complex 3D work is built

items.label: Distant friends and family
items.title: More ways to be together
items.body: People can talk, play, watch, read, rest, or explore without requiring constant conversation or identical attention.

items.label: Interaction designers
items.title: Activities advertise themselves in the world
items.body: Visible objects, carried props, poses, ceremonies, and proximity make participation legible without turning the product into a stack of panels.

items.label: Realtime engineers
items.title: State representation follows behavior
items.body: The architecture demonstrates when to use durable schemas, transient relays, local simulation, peer media, shared timestamps, or staged server authority.

items.label: AI-assisted creative teams
items.title: Visual feedback becomes actionable evidence
items.body: Studios and spatial notes replace ambiguous direction with a reopenable camera, frame, object, coordinate, scene state, comparison, and acceptance record.

pageSections.title: I created the product, integrated the system, and designed how its visual quality is judged
pageSections.markdown: I created Birb Hangout's co-presence premise and experience direction; designed the room, activities, social interactions, Dream, and world; built and integrated the React Three Fiber client, Colyseus server, shared protocol, persistence, media, reading, audio, trivia, flight, terrain, deployment, and service safeguards; directed character and interaction quality; and created the specialist studios, capture systems, spatial annotation, candidate safeguards, and human-controlled evaluation process.

pageSections.title: A playable social world and a rigorous platform for continuing its development
pageSections.markdown:
Birb Hangout implements the private-room journey, persistent identity, shared activities, expressive and consent-based interaction, peer voice, room persistence, the Dream flight system, procedural terrain, development studios, reproducible capture, spatial annotation, and evidence-led candidate review.

The live deployment demonstrates the integrated product on a single service. The next operational studies cover larger concurrency, broader browser and media conditions, and population-level social outcomes.
